newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bell Lines' Rotterdam terminal faces 24 job losses.
newsitem.headline: Bell Lines' Rotterdam terminal faces 24 job losses.

text.p: Bell Lines' Rotterdam terminal will escape the worst of the Irish shortsea shipping line's restructuring plan, Bram Boer, general manager of the terminal told Reuters today.
Some 24 jobs are likely to be cut from the 160 staff employed at the Dutch terminal, Boer said. Job losses will be across the board in both the operations and container transport divisions, he added.

Bell Lines restructuring plan, which is expected to be circulated this week in Dublin, is likely to include job losses of up to 200 across the group's 600-strong workforce. Most of the cuts are expected to hit the company's Dublin headquarters.
Boer said the Rotterdam terminal, which is central to Bell Lines European network, will operate at full capacity next year.
The Dublin-based company has handled 260,000 containers in Rotterdam after just a year of operation, he said. The terminal has a maximum capacity of 300,000 containers a year.
Boer said he expects to announce the arrival of two new customers during the next few weeks.
As well as handling Bell Lines, the terminal also serves Lys Line, Euroline and Geest North Sea Line among other customers.
Irish Continental Group Plc holds a 25 percent stake in Bell Lines.
Press reports from Ireland have speculated that Bell's shareholders will inject between 3.0 million and 5.0 million sterling into the ailing company.

Bell has previously blamed its problems on weather damage to its Belview container terminal in Waterford and tough competition, particularly from the Channel Tunnel which has hit its North Sea routes.
